items.title: Step 1
items.description:
HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. It's the code that defines the structure and content of a webpage. This is your code editor, where you'll write HTML.

Find line 1 in the editor and type this text:

```md
Welcome to freeCodeCamp
```

When you are done, click the "check your code" button to see if it's correct.

hints.text: You should have the text `Welcome to freeCodeCamp` in your editor. Double-check for spelling.

items.title: Step 2
items.description:
HTML is made up of elements. The first one you will use is the `h1` element: ```html

Welcome to freeCodeCamp

``` It starts with an opening tag (`

`), ends with a closing tag (`

`), and has the text it will display in between the tags. Turn your `Welcome to freeCodeCamp` text into an `h1` element by adding an opening tag in front of it, and a closing tag after it.

hints.text: Your `h1` element should have an opening `<h1>` tag.
Your `h1` element should have a closing `` tag.

Your `h1` element should look like this: `

Welcome to freeCodeCamp

`.

items.title: Step 3
items.description:
Notice that the HTML you write in the editor shows up in the preview. In this workshop, you will write the HTML for a partial curriculum webpage.

Below your `h1` element, type the following on the empty line:

```md
Full-Stack Curriculum
```

hints.text: You should have the text `Full-Stack Curriculum` in your editor. Double-check for spelling.

items.title: Step 4
items.description:
An `h1` element is the main heading of a webpage and you should only use one per page. `h2` elements represent subheadings. You can have multiple per page and they look like this: ```html

This is a subheading.

``` Turn the `Full-Stack Curriculum` text into an `h2` element by surrounding it with opening and closing `h2` tags.

hints.text: Your `h2` element should have an opening `<h2>` tag.
Your `h2` element should have a closing `` tag.

Your `h2` element should look like this: `

Full-Stack Curriculum

`.

items.title: Step 5
items.description:
Below the other two lines of text, add:

```md
Learn the skills to become a full-stack developer
```

hints.text: You should have the text `Learn the skills to become a full-stack developer` in your editor. Double-check for spelling.

items.title: Step 6
items.description:
When you need to add a paragraph to a webpage, you can use the `p` element like this: ```html

This is a paragraph element.

``` Turn `Learn the skills to become a full-stack developer` into a paragraph element.

hints.text: Your `p` element should have an opening tag. Opening tags have this syntax: `<elementName>`.
Your `p` element should have a closing tag. Closing tags have this syntax: `</elementName>`.
Your `p` element's text should be `Learn the skills to become a full-stack developer`.
Your `p` element should be below your `h2` element.

items.title: Step 7
items.description:
There are six heading elements in HTML: `h1` through `h6`. They're used to show the importance of sections on your webpage, with `h1` being the most important and `h6` the least.

Below your `p` element, add an `h3` heading with the text:

```md
Introduction to HTML
```

hints.text: Your `h3` element should have an opening `<h3>` tag.
Your `h3` element should have a closing `` tag.
Your `h3` element's text should be `Introduction to HTML`.

items.title: Step 8
items.description:
Notice that each heading looks a little different in the preview. Same with the paragraph.

Next, add another `p` element that displays the following text:

```md
HTML represents the content and structure of a webpage
```

hints.text: You should have a second `p` element.
Your `p` element should have the text `HTML represents the content and structure of a webpage`. You can copy the text from the instructions.

items.title: Step 9
items.description:
You're getting the hang of it. Next, add another `h3` element at the bottom of the editor with the text:

```md
Introduction to CSS
```

hints.text: You should add a second `h3` element to the page.
Your `h3` element's text should be `Introduction to CSS`.

items.title: Step 10
items.description:
While HTML defines the structure and content of a webpage, CSS is used to add style — things like colors, fonts, spacing, and layout.

Below the `h3` you just added, add another paragraph element with the text:

```md
CSS is used to style a webpage
```

hints.text: You should have exactly two `h3` elements, make sure to not remove the existing ones, and to not add new ones.
You should not change the text of the second `h3` element, it should still read `Introduction to CSS`.
You should add a third `p` element to the page.
Your `p` element should have the text `CSS is used to style a webpage`. You can copy the text from the instructions.

items.title: Step 11
items.description:
Finally, JavaScript makes your webpage interactive — it lets you tell the page what to do when someone clicks a button, submits a form, or many other things.

For the last step of the workshop, add another `h3` and `p` element to the page describing JavaScript.

First, add an `h3` element with the text:

```md
Introduction to JavaScript
```

Then, below that `h3` element, add a `p` element with the following text:

```md
JavaScript adds interactivity to a webpage
```

hints.text: You should add a third `h3` element to the page.
Your `h3` element's text should be `Introduction to JavaScript`.
You should add a fourth `p` element to the page.
Your `p` element should have the text `JavaScript adds interactivity to a webpage`
